name: Ritesh Dhekane
headline: I learn the manual mid-flight.

hero.title: Precise software,
hero.line: Full-stack developer. Web apps, SaaS products and AI tools for people who need them to just work.

intro: Give me a problem — a business website, a SaaS product, an AI tool or something nobody has built yet — and I'll figure it out and ship it.
about: I'm a software engineer from Pune. By day I build full-stack features on a B2B SaaS product: Spring Boot services, React and TypeScript screens, PostgreSQL, AWS.
Outside work I build my own products end to end: an HR platform, a fee-collection portal, an AI presentation generator, a mock-interview app, study tools for MCA, BCA and MBA students and more.
I don't wait until I know a tool before starting. I pick the problem, read the manual on the way, and keep shipping in small steps.

experience.title: Software Engineer
highlights: Build full-stack features across Spring Boot services and React/TypeScript apps: REST APIs, database changes and the screens that use them.
Fixed a race condition between third-party webhook processing and internal database transactions using pessimistic row-level locking.
Redesigned multi-provider fallback scheduling so secondary providers are used only after the primary search is exhausted, removing duplicate scheduling.
Applied the Strategy pattern to OTP generation and extended an OAuth2 / AWS Cognito login flow to handle identity-provider challenges.
Added PostgreSQL migrations, S3 presigned-URL uploads and automated tests; integrated a payment gateway into a patient payment flow.
Investigate and fix production issues with senior developers and architects in an Agile team (Jira, GitHub, Bitbucket).

experience.title: Software Engineer Intern
highlights: Built data pipelines with Apache Spark and Azure Data Factory.
Wrote ETL workflows moving large datasets between AWS S3 and Azure Blob Storage.

principles.title: Read the manual mid-flight
principles.text: New tool, new domain, new language: I start with the problem and learn what it needs on the way.

principles.title: Ship small, ship often
principles.text: Working software every few days beats a perfect plan. You see progress, I get feedback early.

principles.title: Leave it documented
principles.text: Every project gets a README, clear decisions and a way to run it, so it isn't stuck with me.

process.text: We talk about the problem, not the tech. 20–30 minutes on WhatsApp or a call.
I write a short plan: what we build first, what comes later, and how we'll know it works.
You see working software every week and can change direction early.
Deployed, tested on real devices, with the handover notes you need.
Fixes and small changes after launch, so you're not left alone with it.
